stem.en: An open economy is one that:

options.en: Uses only domestic currency for all transactions
Trades in goods, services and financial assets with other countries
Has no trade with other countries

explanation.en: An open economy has economic links with the rest of the world: trade in goods and services, flows of financial capital and movement of labour.

stem.en: An Indian buying shares of a foreign company is an example of a linkage through the:

explanation.en: Buying foreign assets (shares, bonds) links economies through the financial market.

stem.en: In the circular flow of an open economy, imports are a:

explanation.en: Spending on imports goes out of the domestic flow of income, so imports are a leakage. Exports are an injection.

stem.en: A nurse from Karnataka working in a hospital in Dubai shows the open-economy linkage through the:

explanation.en: Movement of people across countries to work links economies through the labour market.

solution.en: Movement of people across countries to work links economies through the labour market.

stem.en: Which of the following would make an economy more open?

options.en: Stopping the issue of passports for work abroad

explanation.en: Lower tariffs make trade with other countries easier, increasing openness. The others restrict links with the rest of the world.

stem.en: Balance of trade refers to the difference between:

options.en: Exports and imports of goods only
Exports and imports of goods and services
All receipts and payments with the rest of the world

explanation.en: Balance of trade (BoT) = exports of goods − imports of goods (visible items only).

stem.en: Remittances sent home by Indians working abroad are recorded in the:

explanation.en: Remittances are unilateral transfers (nothing is given in return). Transfers are invisible items in the current account.

stem.en: Which of the following is an invisible item in the balance of payments?

explanation.en: Services are invisibles; rice, crude oil and gold are goods (visible items).

stem.en: Exports of goods are ₹600 crore, imports of goods ₹800 crore and net invisibles are +₹150 crore. The current account balance is:

explanation.en: BoT = 600 − 800 = −200. Current account balance = BoT + net invisibles = −200 + 150 = −₹50 crore.

solution.en: Current account balance = BoT + net invisibles = −200 + 150 = −₹50 crore.

stem.en: The balance of payments of a country is:

options.en: The stock of its foreign exchange reserves
The government’s budget for foreign affairs
A systematic record of all its economic transactions with the rest of the world in a year
A record of only its exports and imports of goods

explanation.en: BoP records all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world during a period, usually a year.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Balance of trade is a broader concept than balance of payments.
Reason (R): Balance of trade records only the exports and imports of goods.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: BoT is narrower; it is only one part of the current account. R is true: BoT covers visible trade in goods only.

stem.en: Foreign direct investment (FDI) into India is recorded in the:

explanation.en: FDI is a flow of financial capital (ownership of assets), so it goes in the capital account.

stem.en: Accommodating transactions in the balance of payments are those that:

options.en: Are undertaken to cover a gap in the BoP, like official reserve transactions
Relate only to exports of goods

explanation.en: Accommodating (below the line) transactions, mainly the RBI’s official reserve transactions, are made to settle the imbalance left by autonomous transactions.

stem.en: A deficit in the balance of payments means that:

options.en: Exports of goods exceed imports of goods
Autonomous payments exceed autonomous receipts, so foreign exchange reserves fall

explanation.en: A BoP deficit is met by drawing down official reserves (or official borrowing), so reserves fall.

stem.en: A country has a current account deficit of ₹120 crore and a capital account surplus of ₹90 crore. Ignoring errors and omissions, its foreign exchange reserves:

explanation.en: Overall balance = −120 + 90 = −30, a BoP deficit of ₹30 crore, financed by drawing down reserves by ₹30 crore.

solution.en: Overall balance = −120 + 90 = −30, a BoP deficit of ₹30 crore, financed by drawing down reserves by ₹30 crore.

stem.en: Which of the following is a capital account transaction?

options.en: Purchase of shares of an Indian company by a foreign investor

explanation.en: Purchase of shares is portfolio investment (an asset flow): capital account. Tea and machines are goods trade, and remittances are transfers: current account.

stem.en:
Which of the following are recorded as inflows (credits) in India’s capital account?
(i) FDI by a foreign firm in an Indian factory
(ii) An Indian firm borrowing from a foreign bank
(iii) An Indian company buying a firm abroad
(iv) Deposits by NRIs in Indian banks

explanation.en: FDI into India, external borrowing and NRI deposits bring foreign exchange in: credits. An Indian company buying a firm abroad is an outflow (debit).

solution.en: FDI into India, external borrowing and NRI deposits bring foreign exchange in: credits.
An Indian company buying a firm abroad is an outflow (debit).

stem.en: If the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per dollar to ₹84 per dollar, the rupee has:

explanation.en: More rupees are now needed for one dollar, so the rupee has lost value: it has depreciated.

stem.en: The demand curve for foreign exchange slopes downward because:

options.en: The RBI fixes the demand for dollars
A higher price of foreign currency makes imports costlier, so fewer dollars are demanded
A higher price of foreign currency makes exports costlier
Foreign tourists spend more when the dollar is dear

explanation.en: When ₹/$ rises, foreign goods cost more in rupees, imports fall and so does the demand for dollars.

stem.en: Which of the following increases the supply of US dollars in India?

explanation.en: Foreign tourists exchange their dollars for rupees to spend here, which adds to the supply of dollars. The others create demand for dollars.

stem.en: The demand for dollars is Qd = 400 − 4e and the supply is Qs = 6e − 100, where e is ₹ per $. The equilibrium exchange rate is:

explanation.en: At equilibrium 400 − 4e = 6e − 100, so 10e = 500 and e = ₹50 per $. (Quantity = 400 − 200 = 200.)

solution.en: At equilibrium 400 − 4e = 6e − 100, so 10e = 500 and e = ₹50 per $. (Quantity = 400 − 200 = 200.)

stem.en: Under a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by:

options.en: The demand for and supply of foreign exchange in the market
The gold content of the currency

explanation.en: A flexible (floating) rate is set by market forces of demand and supply, without central bank intervention.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Depreciation of the rupee tends to increase India’s exports.
Reason (R): Depreciation makes Indian goods cheaper for foreign buyers.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: with more rupees per dollar, a foreign buyer pays fewer dollars for the same Indian good, so exports rise.

stem.en: The movement of the exchange rate described in the passage is:

explanation.en: The rupee lost value through market forces (more rupees per dollar), so it is depreciation. Devaluation is a deliberate official cut under a fixed rate.

passage.en: During one year the exchange rate moved from ₹82 to ₹86 per US dollar. World crude oil prices rose sharply, so India’s import bill went up. Foreign portfolio investors also pulled money out of Indian shares. The RBI sold some dollars from its reserves to slow down the fall of the rupee. Exporters of software and garments, however, were pleased with the change.

stem.en: Which factor in the passage explains why the rupee price of the dollar rose?

options.en: A higher import bill and outflow of portfolio funds raised the demand for dollars
The RBI’s sale of dollars raised the supply of dollars

explanation.en: Costlier oil imports and FPIs taking money out both increase demand for dollars, pushing ₹/$ up. The RBI’s sale of dollars worked in the opposite direction, slowing the fall.

passage.en: During one year the exchange rate moved from ₹82 to ₹86 per US dollar. World crude oil prices rose sharply, so India’s import bill went up. Foreign portfolio investors also pulled money out of Indian shares. The RBI sold some dollars from its reserves to slow down the fall of the rupee. Exporters of software and garments, however, were pleased with the change.

stem.en: The exchange rate rises from ₹75 to ₹80 per US dollar. The rupee cost of importing a machine priced at $200 rises by:
Devaluation refers to:

options.en: A rise in the official value of the domestic currency
A deliberate reduction in the value of the domestic currency by the government under a fixed exchange rate
A fall in the value of the domestic currency due to market forces
A rise in the value of the domestic currency due to market forces

explanation.en: Devaluation is an official act under a fixed (pegged) system. A market-driven fall is depreciation.

stem.en: A managed floating exchange rate system is one in which:

options.en: The rate is largely market-determined but the central bank intervenes to limit fluctuations
The rate is fixed permanently by the government
The rate is linked to gold
There is no foreign exchange market

explanation.en: Managed floating (dirty floating) mixes flexible rates with central bank buying and selling of foreign currency to reduce volatility.

stem.en: Under a fixed exchange rate, to stop the domestic currency from losing value the central bank:

options.en: Sells foreign currency from its reserves

explanation.en: Selling foreign currency raises its supply in the market and keeps its price (in domestic currency) from rising.

stem.en: Which exchange rate system does India follow?

options.en: Purely flexible with no RBI intervention

explanation.en: Since the early 1990s India has had a market-determined rate in which the RBI intervenes when needed: managed floating.

solution.en: Since the early 1990s India has had a market-determined rate in which the RBI intervenes when needed: managed floating.

stem.en: A limitation of the fixed exchange rate system is that:

options.en: The central bank must hold large foreign exchange reserves to defend the rate
It creates great uncertainty in trade

explanation.en: To keep the rate fixed the central bank must be ready to sell foreign currency whenever there is excess demand, which needs large reserves.

stem.en:
Match List I with List II.
List I: (A) Depreciation (B) Devaluation (C) Revaluation (D) Appreciation
List II: (I) Fall in the value of domestic currency by government action under a fixed rate (II) Fall in the value of domestic currency due to market forces (III) Rise in the value of domestic currency by government action (IV) Rise in the value of domestic currency due to market forces

explanation.en: Depreciation and appreciation are market-driven (flexible rates); devaluation and revaluation are official changes under fixed rates. So A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

solution.en: Depreciation and appreciation are market-driven (flexible rates); devaluation and revaluation are official changes under fixed rates.
